source: Based on Pillco Zolá & Bengtsson (2006), Satgé et al. (2019), and field observations

data.label: Stable period
data.description: Lake Poopó at near-full extent during a wet decade.

data.label: First major El Niño
data.description: Strong El Niño event drastically reduces water levels.

data.label: Severe El Niño
data.description: 1997-98 El Niño event causes dramatic water loss.

data.label: Quinoa boom begins
data.description: Increased water diversion for quinoa cultivation begins.

data.label: Near-collapse
data.description: 2014-16 El Niño begins the final desiccation.

data.label: Complete desiccation
data.description: Lake Poopó is declared 'disappeared' by the city of Oruro in December 2015.

data.label: Continued drought
data.description: Only a few centimeters of seasonal runoff water remain.
